board.note: You kept Han Kang off the last board and retired the other eight yourself, so this one is built on two data points rather than one: the lines you take are compact claims about how something actually works, and the lines you add for yourself — Musk on requirements, Cherny on verification — are the same shape. So I went looking for that shape outside the people who build AI. What I found was Meadows arguing that we reliably push the right lever the wrong way, Čapek stating in 1920 the premise the whole acceleration argument still rests on, and a Vatican note from last year making a definitional claim about AI that you can disagree with. Krasznahorkai's lecture is eight months old and is the same size of claim as the Amodei essays you hold, aimed the other way. Two seams I am closing rather than mining again: finance and investing is 0 for 5 and you tombstoned Keynes, Knight, Mallaby and Thiel in one go, and Nordic writing is 0 for 3. Five lines, not nine — I held back a sixth I liked because it would have made three of six from the same source.
